name: Aloo ke Gutke
subtitle: kumaoni boiled potatoes tossed hot in mustard oil, whole chillies and coriander seed

ingredients.qty: 600g, boiled, peeled and cut into 2cm chunks

ingredients.note: stands in for jakhya, the wild hill seed used at home
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Boil the potatoes the day before if you can and refrigerate them. Cold cooked potato holds its shape in the pan instead of mashing.
Break the potatoes into chunks with your hands rather than cutting them. The ragged surfaces catch far more spice.
Have every spice measured out beside the stove — the tempering here takes under a minute from start to finish.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then drop the heat to medium and wait 30 seconds.
Add the cumin and mustard seeds together. They should pop within 5 seconds.
Throw in the broken red chillies and the hing and stir for 15 seconds until the chillies darken a shade.
steps.tip: The chillies scorch fast. Move straight to the next step the moment they change colour.

steps.text: Add the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder, stir once, and immediately tip in the potatoes.
Toss over medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes until the potatoes are patched with gold and crusty at the edges.
steps.tip: Resist stirring constantly. Let them sit still for a minute at a time to build a crust.

steps.text: Add the salt, dry ginger powder, amchur and slit green chillies. Toss for 2 more minutes.
Kill the heat, fold through the coriander leaves and serve hot with plain rice or with a bowl of dal.

storage: Best within a couple of hours. Keeps 2 days refrigerated; revive in a dry pan over high heat rather than the microwave, which leaves them soggy.
